title: Plantar pressure data set

experiment.site: Laboratory of Biomechanics and Motor Control, Federal University of ABC, Brazil
experiment.tasks: Quiet stance and barefoot walking at three self-selected speeds. A subset of 37 participants also ran at a comfortable speed.
experiment.plantar_pressure: Two Zebris FDM-1.5 pressure platforms placed end to end.
experiment.surface_scans: Separate left and right foot and lower-leg scans acquired with Microsoft Kinect and Skanect 1.8.3.

pressure_grid.orientation: Gait y increases in the walking direction. Stance retains the platform orientation.
pressure_grid.time: Trial-relative seconds = frame / frequency_hz. Gait 100 Hz; stance final 100 frames at 10 Hz.
pressure_grid.sparsity: Initialize all n_frames by 353 by 64 cells to zero, then fill the stored readings.
pressure_grid.junction_row: Rows 0-175 and 177-352 come from two 176-row platforms placed end to end. The Zebris software fills row 176 at their junction with the mean of rows 175 and 177, rounded down to the 5 kPa step; those readings count toward force, contact area and the maps.
pressure_grid.edges: During curation, gait steps that loaded row 0 or row 352 were removed, and 1.1.1 removes contacts that load column 0 or 63.

pressure_features.force: Sum of sensor pressures in kPa multiplied by 1000 and sensor area in square metres.
pressure_features.cop: Pressure-weighted mean of the sensor-center coordinates, in the same axes as the pressure grid.
pressure_features.contact_area: Number of loaded cells multiplied by the area of one sensor in square centimetres.
pressure_features.peak_pressure: Maximum loaded cell pressure in each frame and support group, in kPa.
pressure_features.side_assignment: Each retained pressure reading has an anatomical foot side. Gait assignments use acquisition contact marks and reviewed foot regions. For stance the lower of the two occupied x bands is the left foot.
pressure_features.missingness: An unloaded support has zero force, contact area and peak pressure, and null COP.

gait_contacts.walking: Each segmented walking footprint on the original grid defines one contact. The interval spans its first through last loaded frame, including any intervening unloaded samples.
gait_contacts.running: Each uninterrupted run of loaded frames for one anatomical foot defines one running contact.
gait_contacts.numbering: Contacts start at one in order of first load within each trial. The start frame is inclusive and the stop frame is exclusive.
gait_contacts.strike_index: After Cavanagh and Lafortune (1980): the center of pressure at onset, the first frame with at least 20 N on the foot, along the walking direction. The first loaded frame reaches 20 N in 43% of contacts. The footprint is the union of the contact's loaded sensors; its posterior and anterior edges are the outer edges of the lowest and highest loaded rows.

gait_contacts.excluded_note: contact_1_0_0 is the contact number in 1.0.0 and 1.1.0. In the 23 trials where an excluded contact preceded others, the later contacts move up, so their 1.0.0 (trial_id, contact) keys do not match 1.1.1. Footprint numbers shift in the 26 walking groups that lost a contact; in s022 ws R and s084 wc R the excluded contact was the registration template, so every image in those groups changed. All other footprint images are identical to 1.0.0, although some carry new contact numbers. The toe and heel cases reach row 351 or row 2 with the toes or heel missing compared with the participant's other contacts. Kept contacts that reach rows 1-3 or 350-351 are at least 0.93 of the participant's median footprint length for that task and side and show a complete heel and toes. The column rule is conservative: about half of its 40 contacts load the edge column lightly (under 0.5% of their pressure) and look nearly complete. Because excluded contacts can lie between kept ones, 16 trials have two consecutive same-side contacts; check sides before pairing consecutive contacts into steps.
gait_contacts.boundaries: A contact runs from the first to the last frame with any reading on that foot, at the platform's detection limit (5 kPa on one sensor, about 0.36 N). A 20 N force threshold, common with force plates, would shorten a median contact by 10-30 ms (2-4%) and remove about 0.05% of its impulse; the per-foot force in pressure_features gives thresholded times.

joins.pressure: Join pressure or pressure_features to trials on trial_id.
joins.contacts: Join contacts to trials on trial_id. On the original grid, a gait reading belongs to the contact of the same trial_id and side with start_frame <= frame < stop_frame.
joins.footprints: Join registered walking footprint pixels to contacts on (trial_id, contact). Each footprint image represents one walking contact. Its pixel coordinates refer to the registered image.
joins.subjects: Project subject_columns from trials and take distinct rows, one per participant.
joins.contact_maps: Join contact_maps to contacts on (trial_id, contact) and to trials on trial_id.
joins.standing_maps: Join standing_maps to trials on trial_id.

trials.description: Participant characteristics and pressure trial index

trial_id.description: Unique release trial identifier. Join to trials.trial_id.

subject.description: Pseudonymous participant identifier, s001 through s095.

trial.description: One-based trial number within participant and condition.

n_frames.description: Number of recorded frames, including unloaded frames.

n_cells.description: Count of nonzero pressure readings across the trial.

Age.description: subject’s age in years at the data collection, with one decimal place, computed from the dates of birth and of the data collection.

Height.description: subject’s height in centimeters (measured with a calibrated stadiometer).

Mass.description: subject’s mass in kilograms (measured with a calibrated scale).

DominantLeg.description: preferred self-reported leg for kicking a ball (R, L, or Ambidextrous).

PAfreq.description: number of days per week the subject practiced physical activity (from 0 to 7).

PAtype.description: type of physical activity practiced (“None” when PAfreq is 0).

Ortho-Prosthesis.description: whether the subject wears any type of orthosis or prosthesis, as declared by the subject (Yes or No).

Ortho-Prosthesis2.description: name of the orthosis or prosthesis the subject wears (“None” if the subject did not wear any orthosis or prosthesis).

Footwear.description: most common type of footwear the subject wears daily.

FootwearSize.description: size of footwear in Brazilian standards.

FootLenR.description: right foot length in cm (measured with a calibrated caliper).

FootLenL.description: left foot length in cm (measured with a calibrated caliper).

FootWidR.description: right foot width in cm (measured with a calibrated caliper).

FootWidL.description: left foot width in cm (measured with a calibrated caliper).

FootOrthosis.description: type of foot orthosis on shoes (Insoles or None in the released cohort; protocol categories also included rigid orthosis and taping).

Illness.description: whether the subject had any illness at the time of the trials, as declared by the subject (Yes or No).

Illness2.description: type of illness of the subject (“None” when no illness was reported; one participant with Illness = “Yes”, s022, also has “None” here).

Medication.description: whether the subject takes any medication regularly (Yes or No).

MedicationName.description: name of the medication(s) the subject takes (“None” when no medication was reported; one participant with Medication = “Yes”, s095, also has “None” here).

MSKinjury.description: whether the subject sustained a musculoskeletal injury in the 12 months prior to data collection, as declared by the subject (Yes or No).

MSKinjuryNames.description: type of injury(ies) sustained by the subject (“None” if the subject did not have injuries).

Surgery.description: whether the subject underwent any surgical procedures in the 12 months prior to data collection, as declared by the subject (Yes or No).

SurgeryName.description: name of surgical procedure as declared by the subject (“None” if the subject had no surgery).

LegLength.description: leg length in cm (average of the two legs, measured with a metric tape).

BMI.description: body mass index in kg/m² (Mass divided by the square of Height in meters, rounded to 0.1).

AgeGroup.description: age group: Y (younger adults, 18–50 completed years; decimal Age 18.4–50.7) or O (older adults, 59 years or more; decimal Age 59.2–87.1).

TrialsWS.description: number of trials with plantar pressure data walking at slow speed (10 in the protocol).

TrialsWC.description: number of trials with plantar pressure data walking at comfortable speed (10 in the protocol).

TrialsWF.description: number of trials with plantar pressure data walking at fast speed (10 in the protocol).

TrialsRC.description: number of trials with plantar pressure data running at comfortable speed (0 when no running pressure trials are available). Running was performed only by subjects fit enough.

TrialsStanding.description: number of trials with plantar pressure data during standing still (1 for each retained subject; one trial includes both feet).

stop_frame.description: Frame immediately following the last loaded frame, exclusive.

contact_y_max.description: Highest loaded sensor-center y coordinate on the original grid.

strike_index.description: Center of pressure at onset, the first frame with at least 20 N on the foot, measured along y from the posterior edge of the contact footprint, as a fraction of the footprint length (0 heel, 1 toe).

pressure_time_integral.description: Sum of the sensor's pressures over the interval divided by the sampling frequency.

changes: Relative to 1.0.0, 1.1.1 excludes 50 truncated gait contacts with their sensor readings (gait_contacts.excluded), so trials.n_cells, frame features, later contact numbers in the affected trials and footprint numbers in the 26 affected walking groups follow from the remaining readings, and it adds features/contact_maps.parquet, features/standing_maps.parquet and contacts.strike_index (20 N onset). Relative to 1.1.0, which kept all 1.0.0 contacts and used the first loaded frame as strike onset, 1.1.1 supersedes those tables. scans.zip is byte-identical to 1.0.0.

pressure_maps.peak_pressure: Maximum reading at each sensor over the interval, in kPa.
pressure_maps.pressure_time_integral: Sum of each sensor's readings over the interval divided by trials.frequency_hz, in kPa s. Unloaded frames count as zero pressure.
pressure_maps.mean_pressure: Not stored: pressure_time_integral divided by contacts.contact_time for a gait contact or by trials.duration_s for quiet standing.
pressure_maps.gait_interval: The contact's frames [start_frame, stop_frame) and only the contact's foot.
pressure_maps.standing_interval: All 100 frames of the quiet-standing trial and both feet, each sensor labelled by foot.
pressure_maps.sparsity: Each row is one sensor loaded during the interval. Omitted sensors carry no load.
